name: Alzheimer Society of Ontario
description: They run the First Link referral program, support groups, and free dementia education across the province to help you understand what comes next after a diagnosis.

name: 211 Ontario
description: Dial 2-1-1 anytime, in over 150 languages, to get connected to community and government services for dementia care, respite, and financial help near you.

name: Ontario Health atHome
description: This is the single provincial entry point for publicly funded home care — a care coordinator assesses your situation and arranges nursing, personal support, and therapy visits at home.

name: Ontario Health atHome — Adult Day Programs
description: They coordinate supervised daytime programs across Ontario for people with dementia, giving your loved one social interaction and giving you a much-needed break.

name: Baycrest
description: A world-renowned Toronto campus offering dementia day programs, specialized clinics, long-term care, and a hospital focused on older adults.

name: Baycrest — Family Caregiving Innovations
description: The Koschitzky Centre offers free caregiver webinars, practical tools for managing dementia behaviours, and a personalized caregiver resource assessment tool.

name: Circle of Care
description: A non-profit providing personal support workers, meal delivery, transportation, and caregiver support groups across Toronto and Southern York Region.

name: SPRINT Senior Care — Adult Day Program
description: A weekday program in East York where seniors with cognitive impairments enjoy art, music therapy, and gentle exercise while you get respite.

name: SPRINT Senior Care — Caregiver Relief and Support
description: They offer caregiver support groups, respite through their day program, and home-care relief, all facilitated by a registered social worker.

name: Ontario Caregiver Organization
description: A provincial organization with a toll-free helpline, free counselling, e-learning courses, and resources specifically for unpaid family caregivers.

name: Ontario Caregiver Organization — Peer Support
description: They match you with a trained volunteer who has been a caregiver themselves, for regular phone calls and online support groups where you can share your experience.

name: Toronto Seniors Helpline
description: Call this Toronto-only line 365 days a year for crisis support, caregiver resources, and connections to community services, with interpretation available in over 100 languages.

name: Toronto Central Healthline
description: A searchable online directory of every health and community service in Toronto Central, including respite care, day programs, and home care options.
